plan.title: A recovery screenshot and "Not bad!" sent back to back get one reply that uses the photo

context.text: Night 3 done, Yanni. Lights out by 10:45 again tonight.

transcript.text: [photo recovery-screenshot.jpg: a sleep and recovery tracker screenshot for today: recovery 78%, sleep 7h 40m (92% of need), strain 12.4, HRV 64 ms, resting HR 52 bpm] +++ Not bad!

Morning Yanni! Not bad at all. 7h40m and 78% recovery is a solid result for three nights of a steady bedtime 💪 That's last night's sleep, though. Tonight's step still needs its own proof: in bed, phone down, lights off by 10:45 pm, with a selfie in bed. How many hours of sleep are you aiming for each night?

conversation.reason: Exactly one reply covers the photo and 'Not bad!', cites the sleep and recovery numbers, and never claims it can't see the screenshot.
Only one reply, no contradiction or 'ignore those numbers', and it ties the numbers to tonight's 10:45 step, though it adds a follow-up question about hours.

grade.summary: ZOH sent a single reply that used the screenshot's sleep and recovery numbers and tied them to the 10:45 pm bedtime step, avoiding the earlier failure of multiple contradictory replies. The reply is somewhat longer than requested and adds an extra question, which is the main borderline point.
